questions.text:
Inkjet printers use a voltage across parallel plates to aim electrically charged ink droplets at the paper. The plates are 1.00 mm apart.

Draw the field lines between the electric plates and the charge of the top plate.
questions.expectedAnswer: Arrows evenly spaced upwards. One arrow up and negative plate labelled.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Arrows evenly spaced upwards. OR one arrow up and negative plate labelled.

questions.text: Calculate the voltage across the plates when an ink droplet with a charge of 4.80 × 10⁻¹⁰ C is subjected to a force of 9.60 × 10⁻⁴ N.
questions.markingGuide: E = F/Q = 9.6 × 10⁻⁴ / 4.8 × 10⁻¹⁰ = 2 × 10⁶ N C⁻¹ or V m⁻¹. V = Ed = 2 × 10⁶ × 1 × 10⁻³ = 2000 V. Achieved: E calculated correctly. Merit: Correct voltage calculated.

questions.text:
The voltage across the plates is changed to 4000 V.

An ink droplet of mass 1.02 × 10⁻¹¹ kg, carrying 4.00 × 10⁶ excess electrons is released from the negative plate.

Calculate its velocity as it reaches the positive plate.
questions.markingGuide: E = V/d = 4000/0.001 = 4 × 10⁶ V m⁻¹. q = 4 × 10⁶ × 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 6.4 × 10⁻¹³ C. Ep = Eqd = 4 × 10⁶ × 6.4 × 10⁻¹³ × 0.001 = 2.56 × 10⁻⁹ J. Ep = ½mv²: 2.56 × 10⁻⁹ = ½ × 1.02 × 10⁻¹¹ × v². v = 708 m s⁻¹. Achieved: Shows q = 6.48 × 10⁻¹³. OR substitutes into Eqd = ½mv² and calculates v. OR finds v using E as Ep. Merit: Finds v with one error. Excellence: Correct.

questions.text:
A charged ink droplet is held stationary between the two charged parallel plates.

Discuss how it is possible for the ink droplet to be stationary between the plates.

In your answer:
- identify the forces on the ink droplet and their directions
- describe how the forces combine to keep the ink droplet stationary
- explain what type of charge the ink droplet must have to remain stationary.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: One correct statement. OR one force arrow correctly labelled on diagram. Merit: Two linked statements. OR both force arrows correctly labelled and of equal length. Excellence: Full explanation.

questions.text:
An air fryer consists of a heating element, two fans, and a lamp.

In the diagram, the heating element is represented by a rheostat, and the two identical fans are represented by the resistors.

The circuit has a 240 V supply. The rheostat is 1000 Ω and the lamp. The two fan resistors are each 480 Ω.

Initially switch A is closed and switch B is open, so the element and lamp are on, and the fans are off.

Calculate the current in the lamp.
questions.markingGuide: V = IR → I = V/R = 240/1000 = 0.24 A. Achieved: Correct.

questions.text: Use physics principles to explain what adjustment would need to be made to the rheostat's resistance to increase the power output of the element.
questions.expectedAnswer: Decreasing the resistance of the rheostat would increase the current through the rheostat.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Decrease R and 240 V fixed. Merit: Decrease R, 240 V fixed and rheostat gets 240 V.

questions.text:
Both switches are now closed and the heating element set so that it produces 1800 W.

Show that the resistance of the element is 32 Ω.
questions.markingGuide: R of element = V²/P = 240²/1800 = 32 Ω. Total resistance: 1/RT = 1/1000 + 1/32 + 1/(480+480) → RT = 30 Ω. OR: Lamp: V = IR → I = 240/1000 = 0.24 A. Element: P = IV → I = 1800/240 = 7.5 A. Fans: V = IR → I = 240/960 = 0.25 A. Total I = 8 A. In 5 minutes: Q = It = 8 × 5 × 60 = 2400 C. Achieved: Any ONE of: (i), 300 + any calculated current, current through any single branch found. Merit: Correct with one error. Excellence: Correct answer.

questions.text: Calculate how many coulombs of charge are produced by the power supply in 5 minutes.
questions.markingGuide: Total I = 0.24 + 7.5 + 0.25 = 8 A (or from RT = 30 Ω, I = 240/30 = 8 A). Q = It = 8 × 300 = 2400 C. Achieved: Any correct sub-calculation. Merit: Correct with one error. Excellence: Correct answer.

questions.text:
One day, the lamp stops working.

Use physics principles to explain what effect the lamp not working would have on the current in the circuit and the power output of the element.
questions.expectedAnswer: When the lamp stops working, this removes a pathway and increases the total resistance of the...
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: ONE correct statement. Merit: TWO linked statements. Excellence: Full explanation.

questions.text:
A current-carrying wire is placed between the poles of a horseshoe magnet so that the current crosses the magnetic field at right angles. This creates a force on the wire in the direction shown.

Which of the poles labelled A and B in the diagram above is the north pole?

The diagram shows the main features of an electric motor with 40 turns of wire in the coil. The arrow on the diagram shows the 15 N of force acting on the whole side AB when a current flows in the coil.

In which direction is the current flowing in the coil?
questions.expectedAnswer: Current is B to A or equivalent.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Correct current direction. OR force on CD = 15 N down and force on BC = 0 N. OR Force on BC = 0 N.

questions.text:
State the size and direction of the force on:
- side CD
- side BC
questions.expectedAnswer: Force on CD = 15 N downwards. Force on BC = 0 N.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Correct current direction. OR force on CD = 15 N down and force on BC = 0 N. Merit: Force on CD = 15 N down and force on BC = 0 N and correct current direction. Excellence: Force on CD = 15 N down and force on BC = 0 N, correct current direction, and a link to either current is parallel to field for BC or perpendicular for CD.

questions.text: Use physics principles to explain the differences in the forces in part (ii).
questions.expectedAnswer: Maximum force on CD as magnetic field is perpendicular to the current in the conductor.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: One correct statement. Merit: Linked statements. Excellence: Full explanation.

questions.text:
The magnetic field strength is 1.7 T. The length of AB is 50 cm.

Calculate the current in one strand of wire on side AB.
questions.markingGuide: F = BIL → I_total = F/(BL) = 15/(1.7 × 0.5) = 17.6 A → I_coil = 17.6/40 = 0.44 A. OR F per wire = 15/40 = 0.375 N. And 0.375 = 1.7 × I × 0.5. I = 0.44 A. Achieved: I_total = 17.6 A. OR 0.375 N. Merit: I_coil = 0.44 A.

questions.text:
By removing the voltage source, the motor is turned into a generator.

Calculate the speed with which the side AB must be moving to generate a maximum of 12 volts in the entire coil of 40 turns of wire.

(B = 1.7 T, L = 0.50 m)
questions.expectedAnswer: v = 0.35 m s⁻¹ (accept 7.1 or 14.1 m s⁻¹ depending on method)
questions.markingGuide: V = BLv → v = V/(BL × n) = 12/(1.7 × 0.5 × 40) = 6/(1.7 × 0.5 × 40) ... Actually: V = nBLv. 12 = 40 × 1.7 × 0.5 × v. v = 12/34 = 0.35 m s⁻¹. (6V as DC allow 0.18 m s⁻¹). Achieved: 0.35 or 7.1 or 14.1 m s⁻¹. OR (ii). Merit: (i) and (ii). Excellence: (i) and (ii).

questions.text: Use physics principles to explain what position side AB needs to be in to produce the maximum voltage.
questions.expectedAnswer: Max voltage when the coil is in the position shown (horizontal / parallel to magnetic field), as...
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: In the position shown. Merit: Position and some reasoning. Excellence: Full explanation.
